ownership_review: Actual Hyper Service/Incoming Body and TokioIo own HTTP transport; statically compiled C# handlers use the real A06 notification and A07 typed terminal/take/retire bridge. No managed HTTP core or conformance fixture feature substitutes for native I/O.

Native created owners acquire finite permits; raw successful takes allocate wrappers before result transfer; response read sources keep independent Arc ownership; matched module release preserves the creator allocator.

ChargedBytes owns the whole conservative chunk-capacity permit through Bytes::from_owner and every slice/clone. StreamSlot is independently shared by server Body, producer and claimed managed Handler source. Returned NativeBuffer chunks outlive actual host retirement safely.

Header publication and close share the native control gate. Managed control/setup leases prevent host release before new operation setup settles. Close waits callback/native quiet, managed handlers/controls, operation retirement and bounded observer reservations before completing.

Native tasks are actually polled on one per-host current-thread Tokio runtime and one owned OS worker. Retire checks is_finished then joins the actual worker; a timeout never claims join. Unknown worker panic payloads are explicitly quarantined through A05.

QueuedFrame RAII covers both ordinary dequeue and an already-issued Tokio Permit publishing after Body/receiver destruction. This fixes accounting without releasing backing bytes or live-stream obligations early.

CancelAsync keeps application cancellation registrations off the first Dispose/CloseAsync caller and remains a real close obligation. Waiting cancellation only cancels the caller wait; completion/callback failures survive safe drain.
